on House 122, Dong 3 
House Noe 52 Zeng Teh F 


of TSANG VA-Whl aft @) and WANG LIU ZH (+ 2] 
Despite his denials HSU KIEN CHONG, under furhher 


Police 


interrogation adnitted that he was a member of the Chinese 
Communist Party. Although he at first refused to give his 
home address, he later stated that a wireless station 
belonging to the Chinese Communist Party was functioning 
at No. 122 Dong Loh Fang, Washing Road. 

With the assistance of the Municipal Police a raid 
was married out on that address at 10 p.m. on October 8. 
The occupants of the house had probably been Sutera of 
the arrest of HSU KIEN CHONG, as all the wireless outfit 
articles were found packed up into suitcases ready for e 
removale 

In a first floor front room (Plan No. 2, Room "F®) 
and (Photograph No. 8) in places marked by a cross, 
articles of a wireless station which are enumerated in 
Appendix "D", were seized. 

An interior antenna was installed in the first 


floor front room. It was made fast at the window at 


2 tb Ae ae abe 


point "A", passed through point "BN, and was connected with 


the first floor back room (Plan No. 2 and Photo- Nose 8 & 9)- 


“Gx 

The only man present in the house, one Tsang Ya 
wei CHM), wireless operator, who stated that he was 
there in order to remove the wireless sets, was 
immediately arrested. 

Upon being interrogated he at first denied any 
knowledge of the wireless sets found in the house, but 
under further questioning admitted that he was a wire- 
less operator. He stated that he had installed the 
wireless sets in question just for fun. 

After an exhaustive interrogation he gave his home 
address as No. 52 Zeng Teh Fang, Urga Road. 

The latter address was immediately raided by the 
same party, which had carried out the raid on House 
No. 122, Dong Loh Fang, Washing Road. 

While the police was forcing open the door, which 
the occupants of the house were slow to open, suspicious 
noise, coming from the interior of the house, was heard. 
As it will be seen later it was caused by WANG LIU 2Z& 
(female) who attempted to dispose of certain compromising 
documents. 

Having forced their way into the house, the police 
found in a first floor room (Plan No. 3, Room “e"™ snd 
photograph No- 13) in places marked by a cross, suitcases 
filled with wireless sets articles, also ready for 
removal. (Appendix "E"). 

One WANG LIU zu(E#] &) alias HSU LIU ZE(4%$ ¥]®), 
wife of HSU KIEN CHONG, who was found in the premises, 
was placed under arrest. 

Upon being interrogated regarding the noise heard 
py the police, this woman admitted to have made an 
attempt to dispose of a parcel containing communist 
documents by throwing it out of the first floor window 
into the space between two walls, - the wall of house 


No. 52 and that of the neighbouring house. She stated 


a= 
that she did so in order to carry out her husband's 
instructions, who had told her to get rid of the 

papers by any means possible in case of a police raid. 

Photograph No. 17 shows tthat she was doing in 
order to dispose of the documents in question. Photograph 
No. 16 shows the upper edge of the wall enclosing the 
court yard of House No. 52. The parcel which can be 
seen on this vhotograph, shows the place where the parcel 
throvm by WANG disappeared between the two walls. 

In order to recover the documents in question the 
police had to make holes in the basement of the walls 
(vide photographs Nos. 14 and 15). 

F. Arrest of a female named CHANG Kou Sk 46 ) 

A watch kept in the vicinitges of the houses 
raided by the police resulted in the arrest of a female 
named CHANG KCU at 3 pem. on October 9, at No. 122 Dong 
Loh Fang, Washing Road. On the day of her arrest this 
woman refused to give her home address. 

Upon being interrogated, she stated that she had 
been sent to House No. 122, Dong Loh Faung by her employer 
one Li( ) residing at an unknown address in 4ikawei 
(Chinese territory) in order to find out whether the 
occupants of the house in question were still there. 

On the day following the day of her arrest CHANG 
KOU admitted that she resided at House Noe 348 Rue 
Bourgeat stating that her employer and his wife were the 
occupants of Room Noe 7 in that house. 

A search carried out at that address gave no result. 
The chief tenant of the house, Mrs. Le. Stocker, 
Czechoslovakian, informed the Police that on October 2, 
1934, she had let a room on the second floor of her 
house to a Chinese couple, whose names she did not know. 
She stated thatmat «mak these people had hurriedly left 


her place at 11 pem-e on October 9. Mrs. Stocker formally 


identified CHANG KOU AS the "servant of the Li couple. 


~8~ 
Despite of this statement CHANG KOU does not look 
like a servant of the Li couple, but rather like 
their accomplice. Examination of her hands shows 
hat she had never done any hard domestic work which 

house servants are called upon to do. Her hands 

are well cared for and do not show any trace of 
callousness. 


G. Police raid on House No. 3, rassage 106, Route 
Vallon. 


As Hsu Hom: DAH(G % & ) admitted that he had 
another place of residence at No. 3, Passage 106, Rte. 
Vallon, a raid was carricd out on that address at 
11.30 vem. on October 12, 1934, but without success, 
the occupant cf the house having already removede 

when leaving the premises they had not time to 
remove all their property. 

In a back room of the second floor was found a 
box containing 15 communist propaganda booklets in 
Chinese (Appendix "F"). 

Enquiries show that at No. 3, Passage 106, Route 
Vallon, lived a female named TSU NGOUC# 4A’), 
notorious communist, wanted by the Chinese Authorities 


since several years agoe 


CHAPTER 11 


Investigation of the case. 
Enquiries at the banks

Route Magy, was a saving account book No. 3315

to $2,279.81. The chop (exhibit No- 200) used

Articles of the wireless sets seized in Whashing 
and Urga Roads comprise 3 transmitting and 3 receiving 
short wave stations, constructed by technicians of 
parts purchased one by one, permitted to maintain 
communication with the Soviet districts in China. 

They were used chiefly for communications between 
Shanghai and Juiking. 

Two of the transmitting sets permitted to maintain 


‘ communication even with Moscow, direct or through 


‘the medium of radio stations situated on the Soviet 
-: frontier.
